title: Card transactions with fraud flags, September 2026

findings.headline: Fraud is concentrated in night-time transactions
findings.detail: Night (0–5) has a fraud rate of 30.8% across 718 transactions, against 0.3% to 0.7% in other periods. Night is only 7% of volume, yet it looks like the main pocket of risk.

findings.headline: Fraud rate rose sharply in mid-September
findings.detail: The weekly fraud rate went from 0.6% (week of 31 Aug) to 1.7%, then 4.0% and 4.1% in the two following weeks. The final week shows 1.8%, but it has only 727 rows and may be a partial week.

findings.headline: Digital goods, online and low amounts carry the risk
findings.detail: Digital goods has a 20.4% fraud rate (1,130 rows) and Online has 6.3% (3,974 rows), against 0.3% to 0.7% for other categories and 0.3% to 0.5% for Contactless and Chip. The lowest amount band (1.71 to 535.9) is at 11.4%, while higher bands are 0.3% to 0.6%.

findings.headline: Fraud is very high for AE and SG cards
findings.detail: AE has a 28.6% fraud rate (206 rows) and SG has 31% (187 rows). India (93.5% of rows) is at 1.6%, and US and GB are below 1%. These two countries are small by volume but have a high fraud rate.

findings.headline: Data is complete with no duplicates
findings.detail: All 10,260 rows have no missing cells and no duplicate rows. Overall there are 272 fraud cases, a 2.7% rate. These patterns overlap, so the factors may not be independent.

next_steps: Check how far night-time, digital goods, online, AE/SG and small amounts overlap in the same transactions, so you can see which factors matter most.
Consider tighter review or step-up checks (extra verification) for night-time online digital goods purchases, and test the effect on fraud caught and genuine customers blocked.
Find out whether the week of 28 Sep is incomplete, and review what changed from the week of 7 Sep onwards, such as new merchants or rules.

conclusion: The data is clean, and fraud is concentrated in a few pockets: night-time, digital goods, online, AE and SG cards, and small amounts. First, find out how far these overlap in the same transactions, so any checks target the real drivers and not just the visible patterns. The mid-September rise needs a look, but the last week is partial.
limits: This review uses summary statistics only, so it cannot show how these factors overlap, why fraud is higher in these groups, or whether the mid-September rise will continue.
